verses.text: In the seventh year, Jehoiada found his courage. He made an agreement with the commanders of hundreds: Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri.
They went all over Judah and gathered the Levites from all the towns, and the family leaders of Israel. Then they came to Jerusalem.
All the people gathered made an agreement with the king in God's temple. Jehoiada said to them, "Look, the king's son will rule, just as the LORD promised about David's descendants.
This is what you must do. One third of you priests and Levites who come on duty on the Sabbath will guard the doors.
One third will be at the king's palace, and one third at the Foundation Gate. All the other people will be in the courtyards of the LORD's temple.

Do not let anyone into the LORD's temple except the priests and the Levites who are serving. They may go in, because they are holy. But all the other people must obey the LORD's instructions and stay outside.
The Levites must stand around the king, every man with his weapon in his hand. Kill anyone who tries to enter the temple. Stay close to the king wherever he goes."

The Levites and all the men of Judah did everything Jehoiada the priest ordered. Each commander took his men, both those coming on duty on the Sabbath and those going off duty, because Jehoiada the priest had not let any group go home.
Jehoiada the priest gave the commanders of hundreds the spears and the large and small shields that had belonged to King David and were kept in God's temple.
He placed all the men, each with his weapon in his hand, around the king, from the right side of the temple to the left side, near the altar and the temple.
Then they brought out the king's son, put the crown on him, gave him a copy of the covenant law, and made him king. Jehoiada and his sons anointed him and shouted, "Long live the king!"
When Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and cheering for the king, she went to them at the LORD's temple.

She looked, and there was the king standing by his pillar at the entrance, with the commanders and trumpet players beside him. All the people of the land were celebrating and blowing trumpets, and singers with musical instruments were leading the praise. Then Athaliah tore her clothes and shouted, "Traitors! Traitors!"

Jehoiada the priest sent out the commanders of hundreds who were in charge of the army. He told them, "Take her out between the rows of soldiers, and kill anyone who follows her." The priest had said, "Do not kill her in the LORD's temple."
So they grabbed her as she reached the entrance of the Horse Gate by the king's palace, and they killed her there.
Then Jehoiada made a covenant between himself, all the people, and the king, that they would be the LORD's people.
All the people went to the temple of Baal and tore it down. They smashed his altars and idols to pieces and killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, in front of the altars.

Jehoiada put the work of the LORD's temple under the control of the Levitical priests, whom David had organized in groups in the LORD's temple. They were to offer burnt offerings to the LORD as the law of Moses says, with joy and singing, as David had ordered.
He put gatekeepers at the gates of the LORD's temple, so that no one who was unclean in any way could come in.

He took the commanders of hundreds, the important men, the rulers of the people, and all the people of the land, and they led the king down from the LORD's temple. They went through the Upper Gate to the king's palace and seated the king on the royal throne.
All the people of the land celebrated, and the city was calm, because Athaliah had been killed with the sword.
